title: Item 20c · The accessibility target: WCAG 2.1 or 2.2
subtitle: Unclear — two documents disagree. The rulebook (§4, since v0.2, 2026-10-15) targets WCAG 2.1 AA; the brief for this review asks for WCAG 2.2 AA. WCAG 2.2 is W3C's current version (a Recommendation since October 2023): it keeps everything in 2.1 and adds six checks at levels A and AA. I checked the app against them in the code; nothing in this item changes how the dashboard looks. (Code checked 2026-10-23, after merging main)

items.caption: 2. Option B: the six added checks, in plain words, and where the app stands — most are met already; three things to check in phases 3–4 (focus behind pinned bars, the PIN on touch screens, the contact line on the public pages).

footer:
Your choice — one question: which accessibility target?
A · Keep WCAG 2.1 AA. + no change. − an older version than the current standard and than this review's brief.
B · Recommended: WCAG 2.2 AA (picture 2). §4's target becomes 2.2 AA, with the six checks written in plain words; phases 3–5 test them. + the current standard; little extra work, because most checks are met; the review and the rulebook agree. − three things to check, and maybe fix: focus behind pinned bars, the touch-screen PIN, the public pages' contact line.
C · WCAG 2.2 AA plus the AAA target size (44 × 44 px for every control, on the PC too). + bigger targets for older eyes and hands everywhere. − PC screens get bulkier, against §2.1 “No large buttons”; touch screens already have 44 px.
